text:
Kayla M: Quick q — I'm about to land a Terraform change to add capacity reservations for the GPU fleet. Plan is: reserve 1 p4d per AZ, keep an autoscaling spot-backed nodegroup for burst. Want to confirm strategy for: (1) spot bid/maxPrice approach, (2) k8s taints+tolerations for reserved vs spot, and (3) how we wire driver/runtime secrets. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/482

Josh L: SG. Two quick things: reserve per-AZ is good for eviction protection. For spot, we shouldn't set a custom maxPrice — let AWS standard on-demand fallback handle it unless cost spikes. If you do maxPrice, make it >= on-demand or you risk no capacity.

Priya S: Also agree on taints. My suggestion: reserved nodes get taint gpu=reserved:NoSchedule, spot nodes get label gpu=spot. Pods that need guaranteed capacity can have toleration for gpu=reserved. Keeps scheduling decisions explicit.

Kayla M: Example taint/toleration we were thinking: ```yaml
nodeSelector:
  gpu: reserved
tolerations:
- key: "gpu"
  operator: "Equal"
  value: "reserved"
  effect: "NoSchedule"
```
Is that fine?

Marco V: Looks good. For Terraform, we're provisioning capacity reservations via aws_ec2_capacity_reservation (one per AZ) and tagging them with nodegroup id. Remember CRs are per-instance-type+AZ — so make sure the module loops over AZs.

Kayla M: Here's the TF snippet in the PR:```hcl
resource "aws_ec2_capacity_reservation" "gpu_reserve" {
  count                = length(var.azs)
  instance_type        = var.gpu_instance_type
  availability_zone    = var.azs[count.index]
  instance_count       = 1
  tags = {
    Name = "gpu-reserve-${var.env}-${count.index}"
  }
}
```
Any objections?

Josh L: Minor: ensure the nodegroup uses launch template that pins to capacity reservation (use Placement -> CapacityReservationSpecification -> CapacityReservationPreference = "open" and capacityReservationTarget if CR id known). Otherwise CR won't be used.

Priya S: On secrets: we mount nvidia driver credentials and the kms-wrapped license key as a k8s secret consumed by the daemonset that installs drivers. Make sure the secret is created in kube-system and referenced by node bootstrap. Don't put driver creds in instance user-data.

Kayla M: Right. I added a new secret resource in TF: aws_secretsmanager_secret + kubernetes_secret provisioning in the cluster module. infra-bot ran a plan and flagged that the k8s secret creation needs RBAC role binding.

infra-bot: terraform plan for module.gpu_fleet: will add 4 resources, change 1 existing (nodegroup launch_template), and output: capacity_reservations_created = 3

Marco V: For RBAC, create a service account in kube-system with permissions to create secrets (limited) and have the TF k8s provider use that SA via exec/impersonation or a short-lived token.

Kayla M: Cool. One last question: if a reserved CR fails to allocate (no matching capacity), fallback should still spin spot nodes, right? We don't want hard failure.

Josh L: Yes — nodegroup should be spot-backed fallback with mixed instances policy: set on_demand_percentage_for_base_workloads to 0 (or small) and let autoscaler handle scale-up of spot. Have a health check to alert if reserved CRs are unused for >5m.

Priya S: Add an alert to alerting playbook: reserved-capacity-unused and node-affinity-fail. I can add it after PR merges.

Kayla M: Sweet. I'll update the PR with the launch_template capacityReservationTarget change, add taints, and include a note about RBAC for k8s secret creation. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Josh L: Thanks — ping me for a quick review when updated.

Priya S: lgtm after those small changes.

infra-bot: deploy-check: terraform apply queued by kayla — plan id tfplan-2026-03-17-09

Kayla M: Merging in ~30m after CI passes.

Marco V: ETA for full rollout?

Kayla M: Staggered: AZ1 then AZ2 then AZ3, ~10m between each to watch pod placement.

Josh L: Keep an eye on daemonset logs for driver install failures: kubectl -n kube-system logs -l app=gpu-driver -f

Priya S: I'll add the alertrule to paging if driver-install errors >5 in 3m.

Kayla M: Thanks team, closing the loop here.
